items_all.summary: Donald Trump has established a "Super Intelligence Force." "Superintelligence" is his term for artificial intelligence. The unit is led by Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton and other government officials, coordinates with AI companies, critical infrastructure operators, and interest groups. items_all.title: Google researchers find a way to keep self-improving AI agents from memorizing their tests
items_all.summary: Self-improving AI agents tend to memorize their test tasks, so their gains shrink or disappear on new ones. RRSI, a new method from Google researchers, reins in this effect and lifts scores on unseen benchmarks by up to 4.7 points while using about 30 percent fewer tokens than an unregularized version. The article Google researchers find a way to keep self-improving AI agents from memorizing their tests appeared first on The Decoder .
items_all.summary_zh: 自我改進的 AI 代理往往會背誦它們的測試任務，因此在處理新任務時，它們的成效會縮減或消失。RRSI 是 Google 研究人員提出的一種新方法，它能抑制這種效應，並將未見過的基準測試分數提高最多 4.7 分，同時使用的 Token 數量比未正規化的版本少約 30%。〈Google researchers find a way to keep self-improving AI agents from memorizing their tests〉一文最先發表於 The Decoder。

items_all.title: NASA and IBM's open source lunar model turns 17 years of orbiter data into a foundation for lunar science
items_all.summary: NASA and IBM have released the Lunar Foundation Model, one of the first open-source AI models for lunar science. Trained on nearly 2 million tile bundles, mostly from 17 years of Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter data, it cuts the error in predicting polar ice deposits. The article NASA and IBM's open source lunar model turns 17 years of orbiter data into a foundation for lunar science appeared first on The Decoder .
items_all.summary_zh: NASA 與 IBM 推出了「月球基礎模型」（Lunar Foundation Model），這是首批用於月球科學的開源 AI 模型之一。它在近 200 萬個圖塊組合（主要來自 17 年的月球勘測軌道飛行器數據）上進行訓練，降低了預測極地冰儲量時的誤差。〈NASA and IBM's open source lunar model turns 17 years of orbiter data into a foundation for lunar science〉一文最先發表於 The Decoder。

items_all.title: Chinese AI models parrot state doctrine or refuse to answer on sensitive topics
items_all.summary: Chinese AI models often follow the party line on politically sensitive questions, according to an Aleph Alpha study that rated only 17 to 41 percent of answers as balanced. Aleph Alpha sells "sovereign AI" to governments, giving it a commercial interest in distinguishing its models from Chinese competitors. The article Chinese AI models parrot state doctrine or refuse to answer on sensitive topics appeared first on The Decoder .
items_all.summary_zh: 根據 Aleph Alpha 的一項研究，中國 AI 模型在政治敏感問題上通常遵循黨的路線，僅有 17% 至 41% 的回答被評為平衡。Aleph Alpha 向政府銷售「主權 AI」，這使其在將自家模型與中國競爭對手區分開來方面具有商業利益。這篇題為「中國 AI 模型附和國家教條或拒絕回答敏感話題」的文章最初發表於 The Decoder。

items_all.title: Google's new Gemini tiers cut free users to its weakest model and lock $5/month subscribers out of Pro
items_all.summary: Starting in October 2026, Google will cut free access to its Gemini models. Users without a subscription will only get the smallest model, Flash-Lite, while Flash and Pro will be reserved for paying customers. The move could also set the stage for the more resource-hungry Gemini 4 Argon. The article Google's new Gemini tiers cut free users to its weakest model and lock $5/month subscribers out of Pro appeared first on The Decoder .
items_all.summary_zh: 從 2026 年 10 月開始，Google 將取消其 Gemini 模型的免費存取權限。沒有訂閱的使用者只能取得最小的模型 Flash-Lite，而 Flash 和 Pro 則保留給付費客戶。此舉也可能為更消耗資源的 Gemini 4 Argon 鋪路。這篇題為 Google's new Gemini tiers cut free users to its weakest model and lock $5/month subscribers out of Pro 的文章最先出現在 The Decoder。

items_all.title: Google Research Moves Federated Learning Into TEEs: Gboard Now Trains With Externally Verifiable Differential Privacy
items_all.summary: Google Research has unveiled a federated learning system that moves gradient computation from phones into attested server-side TEEs. Access policies are published to Sigstore's Rekor log and the binaries are reproducibly buildable, so central differential privacy can be checked externally. Gboard already uses it for English and Japanese next-word prediction. The post Google Research Moves Federated Learning Into TEEs: Gboard Now Trains With Externally Verifiable Differential Privacy appeared first on MarkTechPost .
items_all.summary_zh: Google Research 推出了一套聯邦學習系統，將梯度運算從手機轉移到經過驗證的伺服器端 TEE 中。存取策略會發布至 Sigstore 的 Rekor 日誌中，且二進位檔具備可重現的建構能力，因此外部可以檢查中央差分隱私。Gboard 已經將其用於英語和日語的下一個單字預測。這篇題為 Google Research Moves Federated Learning Into TEEs: Gboard Now Trains With Externally Verifiable Differential Privacy 的文章最先出現在 MarkTechPost。

items_all.title: Aleph Alpha Releases Kolibri: A 78.1B Open-Weight English-German MoE Model With Only 3.46B Active Parameters
items_all.summary: Aleph Alpha has released Kolibri, a 78.1B-parameter English-German Mixture-of-Experts model that activates only 3.46B parameters per token. It has a 1M-token context and per-request reasoning effort, and its Apache 2.0 FP8 weights run on a single B200 or H200. The post Aleph Alpha Releases Kolibri: A 78.1B Open-Weight English-German MoE Model With Only 3.46B Active Parameters appeared first on MarkTechPost .
items_all.summary_zh: Aleph Alpha 發布了 Kolibri，這是一個擁有 781 億個參數的英德語混合專家（Mixture-of-Experts）模型，每個 Token 僅啟用 34.6 億個參數。它具有 100 萬個 Token 的上下文與每個請求的推理運算量，其 Apache 2.0 FP8 權重可在單個 B200 或 H200 上執行。這篇題為 Aleph Alpha Releases Kolibri: A 78.1B Open-Weight English-German MoE Model With Only 3.46B Active Parameters 的文章最先出現在 MarkTechPost。

items_all.summary: DeepSeek has released official macOS and Windows desktop apps for DeepSeek Harness v0.2, its MIT-licensed agent harness. items_all.title: We're going to need default hard budget caps on pretty much everything
items_all.summary: Here's a product feature which the world is going to need a whole lot more of over the coming months and years: default hard budget caps . I'm talking about the feature of pay-by-usage services and APIs that lets you say "after $X/month, cut this thing off and return errors". These need to be hard limits. Soft caps, "after $X/month, send me a warning email", will not cut it. Coding agents, and personal agents (coding agents wrapped in a less threatening UI), greatly reduce the friction of spinning up code that can do useful things. Sometimes those things cost money - calls to paid APIs, or hosted web applications, or systems that can bill for additional storage and compute. Nobody wants to wake up to an email sent at midnight warning about a budget limit and find that, while they slept, their rogue service had consumed several hundred (or several thousand) more dollars of usage. An argument against this is that businesses don't want their hosted applications to start throwing errors because some budget was exceeded. I expect that most businesses and individuals would prefer errors to a surprise $10,000+ bill. I think hard budget caps need to be the default. If someone wants to live dangerously they should be able to do that, but it needs to be on an opt-in basis. Have a nice, clear checkbox somewhere prominent: Remove the budget cap. My application will not be shut down if I exceed the configured budget limit, and I will be responsible for subsequent charges. The service I most want to see this from is AWS. items_all_raw.title: Google researchers find a way to keep self-improving AI agents from memorizing their tests
items_all_raw.summary: Self-improving AI agents tend to memorize their test tasks, so their gains shrink or disappear on new ones. RRSI, a new method from Google researchers, reins in this effect and lifts scores on unseen benchmarks by up to 4.7 points while using about 30 percent fewer tokens than an unregularized version. The article Google researchers find a way to keep self-improving AI agents from memorizing their tests appeared first on The Decoder .
items_all_raw.summary_zh: 自我改進的 AI 代理往往會背誦它們的測試任務，因此在處理新任務時，它們的成效會縮減或消失。RRSI 是 Google 研究人員提出的一種新方法，它能抑制這種效應，並將未見過的基準測試分數提高最多 4.7 分，同時使用的 Token 數量比未正規化的版本少約 30%。〈Google researchers find a way to keep self-improving AI agents from memorizing their tests〉一文最先發表於 The Decoder。

items_all_raw.title: We're going to need default hard budget caps on pretty much everything
items_all_raw.summary: Here's a product feature which the world is going to need a whole lot more of over the coming months and years: default hard budget caps . I'm talking about the feature of pay-by-usage services and APIs that lets you say "after $X/month, cut this thing off and return errors". These need to be hard limits. Soft caps, "after $X/month, send me a warning email", will not cut it. Coding agents, and personal agents (coding agents wrapped in a less threatening UI), greatly reduce the friction of spinning up code that can do useful things. Sometimes those things cost money - calls to paid APIs, or hosted web applications, or systems that can bill for additional storage and compute. Nobody wants to wake up to an email sent at midnight warning about a budget limit and find that, while they slept, their rogue service had consumed several hundred (or several thousand) more dollars of usage. An argument against this is that businesses don't want their hosted applications to start throwing errors because some budget was exceeded. I expect that most businesses and individuals would prefer errors to a surprise $10,000+ bill. I think hard budget caps need to be the default. If someone wants to live dangerously they should be able to do that, but it needs to be on an opt-in basis. Have a nice, clear checkbox somewhere prominent: Remove the budget cap. My application will not be shut down if I exceed the configured budget limit, and I will be responsible for subsequent charges. The service I most want to see this from is AWS.
